SEC 1

Scope and General Application

General Code
▼
Coverage & In-Service Authority: API 510 covers in-service inspection, repair, alteration, and rerating for pressure vessels and PRDs protecting them in hydrocarbon and chemical process units.
1.1 General Application & Coverage
  • Vessel Types Covered:
    • Vessels constructed to recognized construction codes [e.g., ASME Section VIII, Divisions 1 and 2 only; API 510 does not cover Division 3 high-pressure vessels].
    • Vessels constructed without a construction code (noncode vessels).
    • Vessels approved as jurisdictional-special based on specific design/testing acceptance.
    • Nonstandard vessels: Fabricated to non-recognized specs or customized commercial designs.
  • Asset Status Rules:
    • In-Service: Active equipment in hydrocarbon, refining, and petrochemical service.
    • Temporarily Out-of-Service (Idled/Preserved): Mothballed for future service—STILL FULLY COVERED by API 510.
    • Decommissioned Vessels: Retired and no longer an asset of record from an accounting standpoint—NO LONGER COVERED by API 510.
    • Abandoned-in-Place Vessels: Left on site after decommissioning. They may require ongoing surveillance or risk mitigation to ensure they do not become structural or physical hazards to surrounding operational units.
⚠️ Fundamental Code Precedence Rule (Clause 1.1.1)

ASME BPVC is written for new construction. If an in-service vessel cannot follow the construction code due to its new-construction orientation, API 510 requirements govern. If there is any conflict between the construction code and API 510, API 510 SHALL TAKE PRECEDENCE.

1.1.2 Organizational Intent & Limitations
  • Restricted Access: Application of API 510 is restricted to owner-operators who employ or have direct access to:
    • An Authorized Inspection Agency (AIA)
    • A qualified Repair Organization
    • A qualified Pressure Vessel Engineer
    • Certified Authorized Pressure Vessel Inspectors (certified per Annex B)
    • Qualified Examiners (NDE technicians)
  • Source Inspection Boundary: Does not cover new shop fabrication surveillance at vendor shops (refer to API RP 588).
  • 1.1.3 Regulatory Hierarchy: Prevailing jurisdictional regulations govern, except where API 510 is more stringent than the regulation—in which case API 510 shall govern.
  • 1.2.1 Exploration & Production (E&P): Upstream vessels may follow the alternative rules of Section 9. Except for Section 6, all other sections of API 510 apply to E&P equipment.
  • 1.2.2 Excluded & Optional Services: Exempted equipment is cataloged in Annex A. Owner-operators may optionally include any excluded vessel. ASME Section VIII Div 1 exemptions (e.g., large vacuum flashers) should be evaluated for inclusion based on risk.
  • 1.2.3 Recognized Concepts: Formally recognizes Fitness-For-Service (FFS per API 579-1 / ASME FFS-1) and Risk-Based Inspection (RBI per API RP 580 and 581).

SEC 3.1

Terms and Definitions

Complete Glossary
▼
Standardized Terminology: Complete catalog of all 83 standardized definitions governing legal, technical, and inspection boundaries under API 510.
3.1.1 Abandoned-in-Place
Decommissioned vessel, depressurized, cleaned, disconnected from process/energy sources, and left on site. Not an asset of record.
3.1.2 Alteration
Physical change in any component with design implications affecting pressure-containing capability beyond the data report. Comparable in-kind replacements are NOT alterations.
3.1.3 Applicable Construction Code
Code/standard to which vessel was built, or deemed by owner-operator/engineer to be most appropriate for in-service evaluation.
3.1.4 Authorization
Formal approval by authorized inspector (and engineer when mandated) prior to starting repairs or alterations.
3.1.5 Authorized Inspection Agency (AIA)
Jurisdiction, insurance company writing PV insurance, owner-operator inspection organization, or contracted inspection organization meeting API 510.
3.1.6 Authorized Pressure Vessel Inspector
An individual certified by API under the API 510 program working on behalf of an Authorized Inspection Agency.
3.1.7 Condition-Monitoring Location (CML)
Designated area on a vessel where periodic examinations are conducted to monitor damage type and rate. May contain multiple examination points (TMLs).
3.1.8 Construction Code
Code/standard to which vessel was originally fabricated (e.g. ASME Section VIII Div 1 or 2).
3.1.9 Controlled-Deposition Welding (CDW)
Welding technique used to obtain controlled grain refinement and microstructural tempering of weld metal/HAZ without PWHT (temper-bead / half-bead).
3.1.10 Corrosion Allowance
Additional metal thickness specified in design over minimum required thickness to allow for expected metal loss during operational life.
3.1.11 Corrosion Rate
Rate of metal loss (mils/yr or mm/yr) over a defined interval. Calculated as short-term (ST) or long-term (LT).
3.1.12 Corrosion Specialist
Person acceptable to owner-operator experienced in corrosion mechanisms, metallurgy, materials selection, and monitoring methods.
3.1.13 Corrosion Under Fireproofing (CUF)
External corrosion of passive fireproofing-protected steel caused by trapped water or moisture ingress.
3.1.14 Corrosion Under Insulation (CUI)
External corrosion of insulated equipment resulting from water trapped under insulation or jacketing. Includes atmospheric attack on CS and chloride SCC on SS.
3.1.15 Cyclic Service
Service conditions subjecting equipment to fatigue cracking from repeated variations in pressure, temperature, or mechanical loading (e.g. coke drums).
3.1.16 Damage Mechanism
Deterioration type resulting in metal loss, cracking, or metallurgical property degradation (detailed in API RP 571).
3.1.17 Decommissioned
Taken out of service permanently and no longer an asset of record from an accounting standpoint.
3.1.18 Defect
Imperfection exceeding acceptable criteria of applicable code, requiring repair, removal, or FFS evaluation.
3.1.19 Deferral
Approved postponement of an inspection, test, or repair recommendation past its scheduled due date, governed by technical review and management sign-off.
3.1.20 Design Temperature
Metal temperature used in vessel design per applicable construction code.
3.1.21 Documentation
Recorded information preserving inspection reports, NDE scans, repair histories, MDRs, and calculations.
3.1.22 Due Date
Calendar date established in inspection plan by which an inspection, test, or repair must be completed.
3.1.23 Engineer (Pressure Vessel Engineer)
Person acceptable to owner-operator knowledgeable in mechanical and structural integrity engineering of pressure vessels.
3.1.24 Examination Point
Specific localized point within a CML where thickness readings or scans are taken.
3.1.25 Examinations
Quality control testing functions performed by NDE examiners (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET).
3.1.26 Examiner
Technician performing NDE who does NOT evaluate overall code compliance unless authorized by inspector. Certified per ASNT SNT-TC-1A or CP-189.
3.1.27 External Inspection
Visual inspection of vessel exterior, paint, insulation, supports, foundations, bolting, and grounding while operating or shutdown.
3.1.28 Fitness-For-Service (FFS)
Quantitative engineering assessment per API 579-1 / ASME FFS-1 determining structural integrity of equipment with flaws.
3.1.29 General Corrosion
Corrosion distributed uniformly over a substantial surface area without localized deep attack.
3.1.30 Heat-Affected Zone (HAZ)
Base metal portion not melted, but mechanical properties/microstructure altered by welding heat.
3.1.31 Hold Point
Point in repair or alteration beyond which work cannot proceed until inspected and signed off by the inspector.
3.1.32 Idle
Temporarily out of service, preserved/mothballed for potential future operation. Still covered by API 510.
3.1.33 Imperfection
Flaw or discontinuity noted during inspection that may or may not exceed code acceptance criteria.
3.1.34 Indication
Response or evidence from an NDE method (e.g. UT echo, RT shadow, dye bleed).
3.1.35 Industry-Qualified UT Angle Beam Examiner
Technician qualified via rigorous performance examination (e.g. API QUTE) demonstrating crack detection and sizing competence.
3.1.36 In-Service
Equipment commissioned and placed into active operation, including maintenance turnaround periods.
3.1.37 In-Service Inspection
All inspection, examination, and condition-monitoring performed across operating life.
3.1.38 Inspection
Verification of code compliance performed by or directly supervised by an authorized inspector.
3.1.39 Inspection Code
Short title for API Standard 510.
3.1.40 Inspection Plan
Documented strategy defining inspection types, methods, scope, extent, and schedule for a specific vessel.
3.1.41 Inspector
Authorized pressure vessel inspector certified under API 510.
3.1.42 Integrity Operating Window (IOW)
Established process limits (temperature, pressure, pH, velocity) required to prevent unexpected degradation (API RP 584).
3.1.43 Internal Inspection
Thorough visual/NDE inspection inside an opened, depressurized, gas-freed, and cleaned vessel.
3.1.44 Jurisdiction
Legally constituted government body with statutory authority to enforce boiler and pressure vessel safety laws.
3.1.45 Localized Corrosion
Corrosion confined to a discrete area of vessel surface (pitting, grooving, impingement).
3.1.46 Major Repair
Repair removing and replacing a large pressure-retaining section (replacing a shell course, head, or nozzle > NPS 12). Requires engineer approval.
3.1.47 Management of Change (MOC)
Formal system ensuring changes in process chemicals, operating conditions, equipment, or metallurgy are reviewed prior to implementation.
3.1.48 Manufacturer’s Data Report (MDR)
Official certification document (ASME Form U-1/U-1A) signed by manufacturer and code inspector detailing design, materials, joint efficiency, and testing.
3.1.49 Maximum Allowable Working Pressure (MAWP)
Maximum gauge pressure permitted at top of completed vessel in operating position for a designated temperature.
3.1.50 MDMT / MAT
Minimum Design Metal Temperature / Minimum Allowable Temperature at which vessel can operate safely under design pressure without brittle fracture risk.
3.1.51 National Board (NB)
National Board of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Inspectors.
3.1.52 Noncode Vessel
Vessel not manufactured to an identified national/international construction code and without code symbol stamp.
3.1.53 Nonpressure Boundary
Components not containing pressure (tray rings, baffles, insulation supports, ladders, exterior skirt).
3.1.54 Nonstandard Vessel
Vessel fabricated from nonstandard materials, nonstandard dimensions, or uncertified custom design.
3.1.55 On-Stream
Vessel containing process fluid under pressure or temperature, connected to active process system.
3.1.56 On-Stream Inspection
Inspection from vessel outside while operating (UT thickness, RT, thermography) without opening vessel.
3.1.57 Overdue Inspections
Inspections past their scheduled due date without an approved deferral.
3.1.58 Overdue Repair Recommendations
Documented repair recommendations past target date without approved deferral.
3.1.59 Owner-Operator
Organization that owns/operates vessel, holding overall mechanical integrity responsibility.
3.1.60 Plate Lining
Corrosion-resistant plates welded inside vessel along edges/plug welds to protect base shell.
3.1.61 Postweld Heat Treatment (PWHT)
Controlled uniform heating below transformation temperature to relieve residual stresses and soften HAZ.
3.1.62 Pressure Boundary
Pressure-retaining envelope: shell courses, heads, nozzles, flange faces, covers, and welds.
3.1.63 Pressure Test
Test with liquid (hydrostatic) or gas (pneumatic) at controlled elevated pressure to verify integrity.
3.1.64 Pressure Vessel
Container designed for internal or external pressure containment (cylinders, spheres, towers, exchangers).
3.1.65 Pressure Vessel Engineer
Qualified engineer responsible for mechanical calculations, rerating, and FFS assessments.
3.1.66 Procedures
Documented step-by-step instructions describing how inspection, welding, or NDE must be executed.
3.1.67 Quality Assurance (QA)
Systematic planned actions providing confidence that vessel, repair, or inspection satisfies requirements.
3.1.68 Quality Control (QC)
Physical verification activities ensuring quality parameters are met (measuring dimensions, preheat check).
3.1.69 R-Stamp
Authorization stamp issued by National Board authorizing welded repairs and alterations.
3.1.70 Repair
Work necessary to restore vessel to suitable condition for current design envelope without altering limits.
3.1.71 Repair Organization
Holder of R-stamp, ASME stamp, jurisdiction authorization, or owner-operator repair department.
3.1.72 Required Thickness
Minimum thickness computed without corrosion allowance per code formulas for pressure and mechanical loads.
3.1.73 Rerating
Change in design temperature, MDMT, or MAWP. Requires calculations, inspection, and nameplate.
3.1.74 Risk-Based Inspection (RBI)
Inspection planning combining Probability of Failure (POF) and Consequence of Failure (COF).
3.1.75 Scanning Nondestructive Examination
Examination covering continuous areas rather than isolated points (AUT, PEC).
3.1.76 Same or Similar Service
Service where fluids, process parameters, and metallurgy are comparable enough to expect identical corrosion.
3.1.77 Strip Lining
Narrow alloy strips welded side-by-side inside vessel to create a protective barrier.
3.1.78 Temper Embrittlement
Toughness loss in low-alloy steels (2.25Cr-1Mo) from prolonged exposure to 343 °C to 577 °C (650 °F to 1070 °F).
3.1.79 Temporary Repair
Repair restoring pressure containment until permanent repair is made (fillet-welded patch). Must be replaced at next turnaround.
3.1.80 Testing
Procedures determining behavior under defined mechanical, pressure, or impact conditions.
3.1.81 Tightness Test
Low-pressure test (air/nitrogen/soapy water) verifying bolted joints and gaskets do not leak prior to startup.
3.1.82 Transition Temperature
Temperature range below which metal shifts from ductile to brittle fracture behavior.
3.1.83 VR-Stamp
National Board stamp authorizing an organization to repair pressure-relief valves.

SEC 4

Owner-Operator Inspection Organization

QA Systems & Roles
▼
Management & Quality Infrastructure: API 510 requires owner-operators to maintain a documented QA manual with 15 mandatory elements and defines explicit boundaries for inspectors, engineers, repair organizations, and examiners.
4.1 Owner-Operator Responsibilities & The 15 QA Manual Elements

The owner-operator shall maintain a documented Quality Assurance (QA) Inspection Manual containing 15 mandatory controls:

  • 1. Organization Hierarchy: Reporting structure guaranteeing inspection independence from operational pressures.
  • 2. Records Management: System for documenting and maintaining progressive inspection and quality files.
  • 3. Interval Scheduling: Establishing inspection frequencies and due-date tracking.
  • 4. Roles & Responsibilities: Detailed job descriptions for inspectors, engineers, and examiners.
  • 5. NDE Qualification: Written practice for qualifying examiners per ASNT SNT-TC-1A / CP-189.
  • 6. Drawing & CML Control: System for managing CML records and isometric drawings.
  • 7. Welding & Repair Control: Procedures for welding, hot tapping, and repair execution.
  • 8. Pressure Testing: Safe testing procedures (medium, temperature, venting, relief).
  • 9. Calibration: Periodic calibration and certification of NDE gauges and instruments.
  • 10. Contractor Audits: Qualifying and auditing contract inspection agencies and repair orgs.
  • 11. Approval of Work: Authorization workflows for repairs, alterations, and reratings.
  • 12. Management of Change (MOC): Integration with process and hardware changes.
  • 13. Quality Audits: Internal and external periodic audit procedures.
  • 14. Integrity Operating Windows (IOWs): Implementation and alarm tracking per API RP 584.
  • 15. Incident Investigation: Root cause analysis of pressure equipment integrity failures per API RP 585.
4.2 through 4.6 Personnel Roles & Boundaries
  • Pressure Vessel Engineer (4.2): Reviews and approves designs, calculations, reratings, FFS assessments, CDW procedures, and authorizes alterations and major repairs.
  • Repair Organization (4.3): Must hold an ASME Code Stamp, National Board R-Stamp, jurisdiction recognition, or be an approved owner-operator repair group. Uses ASME Section IX WPS/PQR.
  • Authorized Inspector (4.4): Holds active API 510 certification. Authorizes repairs and alterations prior to work, designates mandatory hold points, reviews examiner NDE reports, and signs off on completed repairs.
  • Examiners (4.5): Performs NDE (UT, RT, MT, PT). Must be qualified per ASNT. Does NOT evaluate overall code compliance. Angle-beam ultrasonic detection/sizing of planar cracks requires an Industry-Qualified UT Angle Beam Examiner.
  • 4.7 Audits: Owner-operator inspection systems must be periodically audited (recommended every 3 years).
SEC 5

Inspection, Examination, and Pressure-Testing Practices

Field Practices & NDE
▼
Core In-Service Examination Methodologies: Governs inspection plans, RBI methodologies, damage mechanism classification, internal/on-stream/external procedures, CML placement, scanning NDE, hydrostatic/pneumatic test rules, in-service weld examinations, flanged joint integrity, and heat exchanger inspections.
5.1 Inspection Plans, 5.2 Risk-Based Inspection (RBI) & 5.3 Preparation
  • 5.1 Inspection Plan Mandate: An active, equipment-specific inspection plan shall be developed for all operating pressure vessels and PRDs. Plans must identify credible damage mechanisms, extent of examination, CML locations, required NDE methods, and scheduled interval due dates.
  • 5.2 Risk-Based Inspection (RBI): Implemented in accordance with API RP 580/581. Systematically evaluates Probability of Failure (POF) and Consequence of Failure (COF) to determine inspection focus and intervals.
  • 5.3 Preparation for Inspection:
    • Safety & Isolation: Confined space entry authorization, positive isolation (blinding/disconnection), purging, and atmospheric gas testing (oxygen, flammables, toxics).
    • Cleaning: Removal of internal scale, coke, sludge, and process deposits to expose bare metal for visual and NDE examination.
    • Pyrophoric Scale Management: Iron sulfide (FeS) deposits in sour services are pyrophoric; internal surfaces must be kept continuously wet during vessel opening and gas-freeing to prevent spontaneous auto-ignition upon contact with air.
5.4 Inspection for Damage Mechanisms & Failure Modes (API RP 571 Cross-Reference)

Clause 5.4.1 organizes credible damage mechanisms into six distinct physical classifications:

  • a) General & Localized Metal Loss / Pitting:
    • High-Temperature / Refinery: Sulfidation and high-temperature H2S/H2 corrosion (refer to API RP 571 and API RP 939-C); oxidation at high temperatures; naphthenic acid corrosion in crude distillation units.
    • Environmental / Water: Microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC); cooling water corrosion; boiler water and steam condensate corrosion; atmospheric corrosion; soil corrosion at soil-to-air interfaces.
    • Chemical & Salts: Ammonium bisulfide (NH4HS), ammonium chloride (NH4Cl), and amine hydrochloride corrosion; CO2 corrosion (sweet corrosion in E&P).
    • Mechanical Metal Loss: Erosion, erosion-corrosion, and galvanic corrosion between dissimilar metals.
  • b) Surface-Connected Cracking:
    • Fatigue: Mechanical fatigue from cyclic vibration/pulsation and thermal fatigue from thermal cycling.
    • Environmental Stress Cracking: Caustic stress corrosion cracking (caustic embrittlement); polythionic acid stress corrosion cracking (PTA-SCC) during turnarounds; sulfide stress cracking (SSC) in wet H2S services; chloride stress corrosion cracking (Cl-SCC) in austenitic stainless steels.
  • c) Subsurface Cracking:
    • Wet H2S Damage: Hydrogen-induced cracking (HIC) and stress-oriented hydrogen-induced cracking (SOHIC) occurring in carbon steels exposed to sour environments.
  • d) High-Temperature Microfissuring & Macrocracking:
    • High-Temperature Hydrogen Attack (HTHA): Evaluated per API RP 941 (Nelson curves); causes methane bubble formation, microvoid coalescence, decarburization, and internal fissuring.
    • Creep & Stress Rupture: Time-dependent deformation and cavity formation at elevated temperatures exceeding creep threshold.
  • e) Metallurgical Changes:
    • Graphitization: Carbon steel operating long-term above 427 °C (800 °F) converting iron carbide into nodular graphite, causing severe embrittlement.
    • Temper Embrittlement: Toughness loss in 2.25Cr-1Mo and low-alloy steels exposed to 343 °C to 577 °C (650 °F to 1070 °F).
    • Hydrogen Embrittlement: Loss of ductility and cracking under ambient temperature and high stress following atomic hydrogen absorption.
  • f) Blistering:
    • Hydrogen blistering caused by atomic hydrogen diffusing into steel laminations and combining into molecular gas (H2) under extreme internal pressure.
  • 5.4.4 Cyclic Service Evaluation: Vessels in pressure and/or thermal cyclic service must be evaluated for fatigue failure modes, reviewing original code fatigue design criteria, nozzle attachments, and geometric stress raisers.
5.5 Types of Inspection and Surveillance for Pressure Vessels
  • 5.5.2 Internal Inspection: Direct visual examination of 100% accessible inner surfaces, shell, heads, nozzles, and weld seams. Weep holes on reinforcing pads and lined vessels must remain completely open and unobstructed to detect inner envelope leaks.
  • 5.5.3 On-Stream Inspection: Performed from exterior while operating. Allowed in lieu of internal inspection ONLY if: remaining life exceeds 10 years, corrosion is uniform and low, operating environment has been confirmed for ≥ 5 years, operating temperature is below creep range, and vessel has no internal strip lining that could fail behind the lining.
  • 5.5.4 External Inspection: Visual examination of exterior insulation, fireproofing, structural supports, skirts, anchor bolts, grounding, nozzles, flanges, and PRD discharge piping.
  • 5.5.5 Thickness Measurement Inspection: Point vs scanning thickness measurements.
  • 5.5.6 Corrosion Under Insulation (CUI):
    • Carbon & Low-Alloy Steels: -4 °C to 175 °C (25 °F to 350 °F), with peak severity at 60 °C to 120 °C (140 °F to 250 °F).
    • Austenitic Stainless Steels: 60 °C to 205 °C (140 °F to 400 °F) susceptible to External Chloride Stress Corrosion Cracking (ECSCC).
    • Susceptible Locations: Insulation terminations, support penetrations, nozzles, and deadlegs.
5.6 Condition-Monitoring Locations (CMLs)
  • 5.6.1 & 5.6.2 CML Examinations: CMLs are designated areas where periodic examinations monitor damage presence and rate. Representative monitoring is required on all major components (shells, heads, cone transitions) and a representative sample of vessel nozzles. Higher consequence vessels have more CMLs and are monitored more frequently.
  • Scanning vs Point Readings (5.6.2.3): Scanning NDE (profile RT, density RT, automated ultrasonic scanning) must be used where localized thinning is expected to find the thinnest point.
  • Thickness Grids (5.6.2.4): Where detailed FFS metal loss evaluations are needed, thickness grids must be prepared in accordance with API 579-1 / ASME FFS-1.
  • Permanent Marking (5.6.2.5): CMLs and inspection points permanently marked on drawings and equipment for repeatable readings.
5.7 Condition-Monitoring Methods & ASME Section V Examination Matrix
  • Magnetic Particle Testing (MT): ASME Code, Section V, Article 7. Detects surface and near-surface cracks and elongated discontinuities in ferromagnetic materials.
  • Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT): ASME Code, Section V, Article 6. Visible or fluorescent dye penetrant for detecting surface-breaking cracks, pinholes, and porosity in nonmagnetic materials.
  • Radiographic Testing (RT): ASME Code, Section V, Article 2. Profile radiography for component wall thickness and internal volumetric weld imperfections (slag, porosity, cracks).
  • Ultrasonic Testing (UT): ASME Code, Section V, Articles 4, 5, and 23. Digital thickness measurement, shear wave angle-beam for planar flaws, and advanced scanning (TOFD and PAUT per API RP 941 for HTHA).
  • Alternating Current Field Measurement (ACFM / ACFL): Detects and sizes surface-breaking cracks through paint, coatings, and scale without surface cleaning.
  • Eddy Current Testing (ET): ASME Code, Section V, Article 8. Surface-breaking crack detection and tubular examination in heat exchangers.
  • Field Metallographic Replication (FMR): In-situ microstructural replication for identifying creep voids, microfissuring, and graphitization.
  • Acoustic Emission (AE): ASME Code, Section V, Article 12. Structural monitoring of stress waves emitted during controlled pressure loading to detect active flaw growth.
  • Infrared Thermography: Identifies internal refractory lining degradation, thermal bypass, and process fluid levels.
  • Portable Hardness Testing: Measures surface hardness to verify heat treatment (PWHT), cold-work effects, and material substitutions.
  • 5.7.1.2 Surface Preparation Standards: Wire brushing, grit blasting, high-pressure water blasting, chipping, grinding, and chemical etching required as appropriate prior to NDE.
5.8 Pressure Testing Requirements (Hydrostatic & Pneumatic)

Conducted when required by inspector/engineer, and mandatory following major repairs or alterations.

Hydrostatic Test Pressure Equation (Post-1999 ASME Section VIII Div 1):
Ptest = 1.3 × MAWP × (Stest / Sdesign)
Where Stest = allowable stress at test temp, Sdesign = allowable stress at design temp. Ratio is the lowest of all component materials. (Pre-1999 factor was 1.5 × MAWP).
Pneumatic Test Pressure Equation (ASME Section VIII Div 1):
Ppneumatic = 1.1 × MAWP × (Stest / Sdesign)
Requires stepped pressure increase (50% test pressure, then 10% increments), exclusion zones, and engineering review due to compressed gas energy.
⚠️ Test Temperature & Brittle Fracture Prevention (Clause 5.8.7.2)
  • For vessels with wall thickness ≤ 50 mm (2 in.): Metal test temperature must be maintained at least 17 °C (30 °F) above MDMT.
  • For vessels with wall thickness > 50 mm (2 in.): Metal test temperature must be maintained at least 6 °C (10 °F) above MDMT.
  • Relief Protection: Pressure relief device protecting the test system shall be set at test pressure or not more than 110% of test pressure (or test pressure + 10 psi, whichever is greater).
5.9 to 5.12 Materials, In-Service Welds, Flanged Joints & Exchangers
  • 5.9 Material Verification & Traceability: Positive Material Identification (PMI) conducted per API RP 578 on replacement parts, alloy welds, and pressure-retaining fasteners.
  • 5.10 Inspection of In-Service Welds:
    • Welds and heat-affected zones (HAZ) must be examined for preferential weld corrosion and service-induced environmental cracking.
    • When preferential corrosion or cracking is detected, additional welds must be inspected to establish overall damage extent.
    • Crack-like flaws detected in existing welds must be evaluated by the inspector and an engineer or corrosion specialist per API 579-1 / ASME FFS-1, determining whether flaws originated from fabrication or in-service cracking.
    • Dissimilar Metal Welds (DMW) have heightened susceptibility to thermal fatigue and galvanic cracking; inspection plans must include specialized NDE for DMWs.
  • 5.11 Inspection & Repair of Flanged Joints:
    • Visual examination for leakage, staining, and fastener corrosion.
    • Thread Engagement Rule: Fasteners shall be fully engaged for the full depth of the nut on new and reassembled joints. On existing joints, lack of complete engagement is acceptable if not more than one thread is short of full engagement!
    • Gasket seating surfaces must be inspected for distortion and damage per ASME PCC-1 Appendix D before placing back in service.
    • Clamped flanged joints pumped with sealant require ultrasonic bolt examination prior to repumping to verify bolt integrity under process exposure (ASME PCC-2).
  • 5.12 Shell & Tube Heat Exchangers:
    • Inspection of tubesheets, floating head covers, baffles, and shell bundle impingement areas.
    • Tube inspection methods: Internal Rotary Inspection System (IRIS), Eddy Current Testing (ECT), Remote Field Testing (RFT), and Magnetic Flux Leakage (MFL).
SEC 6

Interval/Frequency and Extent of Inspection

Inspection Intervals
▼
Mandatory Inspection Frequencies & Deferral Controls: Establishes statutory maximum inspection intervals, installation baseline requirements, RBI interval extension rules, PRD overhaul frequencies, and the strict two-tier inspection and repair recommendation deferral protocols.
6.1 General & 6.2 Installation and Service Changes
  • New Installations: Baseline thickness measurements and external inspection must be conducted prior to initial operation, verifying Manufacturer's Data Report (ASME Form U-1) and nameplate stamping.
  • Service Changes: Prior to changing process fluids or operating parameters, an MOC review must evaluate new damage mechanisms; inspection intervals and CML locations must be updated accordingly.
6.3 Risk-Based Inspection (RBI) Interval Rules
  • An RBI assessment conducted in accordance with API RP 580 may establish inspection intervals exceeding the limits of 6.4 and 6.5.
  • External Inspection Ceiling: RBI intervals for external visual inspection shall NOT exceed 10 years!
  • 10-Year Re-review Mandate: When an RBI interval for internal or on-stream inspection exceeds 10 years, the RBI assessment shall be reviewed and approved by the engineer and inspector at intervals not to exceed 10 years (or sooner if process or consequence changes occur).
  • PRD Review: When RBI extends vessel internal intervals, the assessment must explicitly include inspection history and fouling tendencies of the vessel's PRDs.
6.4 External & 6.5 Internal, On-Stream and Thickness Intervals
  • External Inspection (6.4): Shall not exceed the lesser of 5 years or the required internal/on-stream inspection interval. Performed while operating. Vessels in noncontinuous service have identical external intervals. Abandoned-in-place vessels require periodic external surveillance.
  • Internal or On-Stream Inspection (6.5): Shall not exceed one-half of remaining corrosion-rate life, or 10 years, whichever is less!
  • Short Remaining Life Rule: Whenever remaining life is less than 4 years, the inspection interval may be the full remaining life up to a maximum of 2 years.
  • Thickness Measurement Interval: Shall not exceed the lesser of half remaining life or 10 years (or 2 years if remaining life < 4 years).
  • Accelerated / Unstable Corrosion: When corrosion accelerates unexpectedly, an investigation consistent with API RP 585 must determine the root cause and update intervals.
6.6 Pressure-Relieving Devices (PRDs) Testing Frequencies
  • Standard Process Service: PRDs shall be tested and overhauled at intervals not exceeding 5 years.
  • Clean, Non-Corrosive Service: PRD test intervals may be extended up to 10 years based on documented clean testing history and absence of fouling.
  • Rupture Disks: Inspected every 5 years or at PRD intervals; replaced per manufacturer recommendations or following any relief event.
6.7 Deferral of Inspections, Tests, and Examinations (Two Tiers)
  • Tier 1: Short-Term Deferral (6.7.1):
    • Duration: Up to 6 months or 10% of interval, whichever is shorter.
    • Justification: Documented technical review confirming safe operation through extension.
    • Approval: Must be approved by the Authorized Inspector AND Operations/Maintenance Management.
  • Tier 2: Long-Term Deferral (6.7.2):
    • Duration: Exceeding 6 months or 10% of interval.
    • Justification: Formal documented Risk Assessment by Pressure Vessel Engineer and Inspector.
    • Approval: Mandatory approval by Executive / Senior Plant Management (Refinery Manager / VP).
6.8 & 6.9 Deferral and Review of Inspection Repair Recommendations
  • 6.8 Deferral of Repair Recommendation Due Dates:
    • Recommendations that cannot be completed by their target due date can be deferred for a specific period by a documented change of date.
    • Must have written concurrence from both the Authorized Inspector AND Inspection Supervisor.
    • Unapproved overdue recommendations are strictly prohibited by code.
    • Deferrals must be the occasional exception, not standard practice. Vessel must remain within code minimum required thickness throughout deferral.
  • 6.9 Review of Inspection Repair Recommendations:
    • Inspector recommendations may only be changed or deleted after review by a Pressure Vessel Engineer or Inspection Supervision.
    • Inspection records must permanently document the technical reasoning, date of change/deletion, and identity of the reviewer.
SEC 7

Inspection Data Evaluation, Analysis, and Recording

Engineering Calculations
▼
Quantitative Engineering Evaluation: Governing mathematical formulas for corrosion rates, remaining life, MAWP determination, Local Thin Area (LTA) averaging, critical length $L$, pitting limits, Table 1 $K_1$ factor, API 579-1 FFS assessments, minimal documentation evaluations (Table 2 design margin history), and permanent/progressive records management.
7.1 Corrosion Rate & 7.2 Remaining Life Formulas
Long-Term (LT) Corrosion Rate (Formula 3):
CR(LT) = (tinitial − tactual) / Time between tinitial and tactual (years)
Short-Term (ST) Corrosion Rate (Formula 4):
CR(ST) = (tprevious − tactual) / Time between tprevious and tactual (years)
Remaining Life (Clause 7.2):
Remaining Life = (tactual − trequired) / CR

Corrosion Rate Selection Factors (7.1.1.2): General vs localized patterns, fluid impingement areas, initiation timing, process upsets (water wetting, chlorides, lower pH), scale formation/stripping, and stagnant deadlegs.

7.3 Maximum Allowable Working Pressure (MAWP) Determination
MAWP = (S × E × tcorroded) / (R + 0.6 × tcorroded)
Where S = code allowable stress, E = weld joint efficiency, tcorroded = actual thickness minus future corrosion allowance, R = inside radius. Static head of liquid must be included where applicable.
7.4 Analysis of Corroded Regions (Averaging & Critical Length L)
  • 7.4.2 Local Thin Areas (LTA) Critical Length L for Cylindrical Shells:
    • For inside diameter D ≤ 1500 mm (60 in.): L = lesser of D/2 or 20 in. (500 mm).
    • For inside diameter D > 1500 mm (60 in.): L = lesser of D/3 or 40 in. (1000 mm).
    • Alternative formula: L = 1.12 √(D × t).
  • Weld Joint Efficiency Effect: If the corroded area does not touch a weld and is at least 25 mm (1 in.) or 2t away from a weld seam, joint efficiency E may be taken as 1.0! Otherwise, actual seam efficiency E must be used.
7.4.3 Pitting Evaluation Criteria:

Widely scattered pits may be ignored if ALL 3 code rules are satisfied:

  • Rule 1 (Depth): Max pit depth ≤ 0.5 × trequired (exclusive of corrosion allowance).
  • Rule 2 (Area): Cumulative area of pits deeper than corrosion allowance ≤ 45 cm² (7 in.²) in any 200 mm (8 in.) diameter circle.
  • Rule 3 (Line Length): Cumulative length of pits along any 200 mm (8 in.) straight line ≤ 50 mm (2 in.).
Table 1: Spherical Radius Factor K1 for Formed Heads

For corroded areas in the central 80% of an ellipsoidal or torispherical head, crown radius R = K1 × D:

Ratio D / (2h)K1 FactorHead Geometry Profile
3.01.84Very shallow formed head
2.81.64Shallow head
2.61.46Flattened profile
2.41.30Intermediate profile
2.21.15Intermediate profile
2.01.00Standard 2:1 ASME Ellipsoidal Head (R = D)
1.80.88Deep ellipsoidal head
1.60.77Deep ellipsoidal head
1.40.67Deep profile
1.20.59Near hemispherical
1.00.50Standard Hemispherical Head (R = 0.5D)
7.5 Fitness-For-Service (FFS) Evaluations (API 579-1 / ASME FFS-1)

Components found with damage affecting load-carrying capacity may be evaluated per API 579-1 / ASME FFS-1:

  • Metal Loss Exceeding CA: Evaluated using future corrosion allowances established per Section 6. Blend-ground areas must have smooth transition radii without sharp corners to avoid stress concentrations.
  • Blisters, Laminations & HIC/SOHIC: Evaluated per API 579-1 Parts 5 and 7, considering pressure, future corrosion, and blister venting.
  • Weld Misalignment & Shell Distortion: Evaluated per Part 8 for allowable peaking, banding, and angular distortion.
  • Crack-Like Flaws: Evaluated per Part 9. Angle-beam ultrasonic sizing of planar crack dimensions requires an Industry-Qualified UT Angle Beam Examiner.
  • Creep, Fire Damage, Dents & Gouges: Evaluated per Parts 10, 11, 12, and 14 for remaining structural life.
7.7 Evaluation of Existing Equipment with Minimal Documentation

For unbranded vessels lacking design data and MDRs, operational integrity is evaluated using Table 2 design margins:

Construction Code & EraDesign Margin (Safety Factor)Basis on Tensile Strength
ASME Prior to 19505.05:1 on ultimate tensile strength
ASME 1950 through 1999 (Pre-1999 Addenda)4.04:1 on ultimate tensile strength
ASME 1999 Addenda to Present (Division 1)3.53.5:1 on ultimate tensile strength
ASME Section VIII Division 23.0 (or 2.4 under 2007+)Engineered allowable stress
  • Unknown Material: Assume lowest structural grade steel: tensile strength Su = 40,000 psi (275 MPa).
  • Unknown Joint Efficiency: Default joint efficiency E = 0.70 (visual exam only).
7.8 Reports and Records Management
  • Permanent Records (Life of Vessel): Maintained throughout equipment service life: Manufacturer's Data Reports (Form U-1), fabrication drawings, heat treatment charts, design calculations, PRD sizing calculations, and baseline inspection reports.
  • Progressive Records (Regularly Updated): Inspection reports, CML thickness updates, repair/alteration records (Annex D), MOC documentation, IOW alarm exceedance logs, and RBI updates.
  • 4 Mandatory Information Types (7.8.2):
    1. Construction and design information.
    2. Inspection history and recommendation tracking.
    3. Repair, alteration, and rerating certificates.
    4. FFS assessment documentation.
  • 90-Day IDMS Posting Rule (7.8.4): Documented inspection results shall be approved by the responsible inspector/engineer and posted into the inspection data management system (IDMS) within 90 days of inspection completion or startup!
SEC 8

Repairs, Alterations, and Rerating of Pressure Vessels and PRDs

Welding & Rerating
▼
Fabrication & Rerating Rules: Governs repair vs alteration authorizations, temporary patches, permanent insert plates, welder qualification, welding procedures, hot tapping rules, PWHT alternatives (Preheat & CDW with Table 3), brittle fracture prevention, and rerating criteria.
8.1 Authorizations & General Rules
  • Repairs: Must be authorized by the Authorized Inspector prior to starting work.
  • Alterations: Must be authorized by BOTH the Authorized Inspector AND the Pressure Vessel Engineer prior to starting work.
  • Hold Points: The inspector designates mandatory inspection hold points during repair/alteration execution.
8.2 Temporary Repairs & 8.3 Permanent Repairs
  • Fillet-Welded Patches (8.2):
    • Must be designed by an engineer for full membrane stress.
    • Must have rounded corners with minimum radius of 25 mm (1 in.).
    • Weld must be a full-circumferential fillet weld.
    • Prohibited in crack-susceptible environments (caustic, amine, wet H2S) unless specifically engineered.
    • Must be replaced with permanent repairs at next planned shutdown.
  • Permanent Repairs (8.3): Flush insert plates require full-penetration groove welds, 100% volumetric NDE (RT or UT), and rounded corners (minimum 25 mm / 1 in. radius).
8.4 Welding and Hot Tapping
  • ASME Section IX Qualifications: Welder Performance Qualifications (WPQ) and Welding Procedure Specifications (WPS) supported by Procedure Qualification Records (PQR) must comply with ASME Section IX.
  • Mandatory Pre-Welding Records (8.4.2.2): Repair organizations must provide WPS, PQR, WPQ, welder continuity logs, and weld maps before welding begins.
  • Preheating (8.4.3): Preheat temperature must satisfy applicable construction code and WPS. Cooler preheat requires engineer approval and a new qualified WPS.
  • Hot Tapping (8.4.1): On-stream welding and hot tapping must comply with API RP 2201 and ASME PCC-2 Article 210, verifying minimum remaining thickness, flow velocities, and avoiding burn-through.
8.5 PWHT & 8.6 Alternatives to PWHT (Preheat & Controlled-Deposition Welding)
  • Local PWHT (8.5.2): May be substituted for 360° banding if engineered procedure evaluates base metal thickness, thermal decay gradients, distortions, full penetration welds, and preheat of 150 °C (300 °F).
  • Method 1: Preheat Method (8.6.1):
    • Materials: P-No. 1 (Gr 1-3) and P-No. 3 (Gr 1-2).
    • Preheat: Maintain minimum 150 °C (300 °F) during welding. Maximum interpass 315 °C (600 °F).
    • Band: Preheat zone extends minimum 100 mm (4 in.) or 4t on each side of weld groove.
  • Method 2: Controlled-Deposition Welding - CDW (8.6.2):
    • Materials: P-No. 1, P-No. 3, and P-No. 4 steels. SMAW, GMAW, GTAW with temper-bead or half-bead technique.
    • Notch Toughness Mandate: Charpy V-Notch impact testing is mandatory on PQR to verify HAZ toughness at MDMT!
Table 3: Qualification Limits for Base Metal & Weld Thickness for CDW:
Welding Test Coupon Thickness (T)Qualified Base Metal Thickness RangeQualified Weld Deposit Thickness
T < 25 mm (1 in.)T to 2Tt to 2t
25 mm ≤ T < 50 mm (1 in. to 2 in.)25 mm (1 in.) to 2Tt to 2t
T ≥ 50 mm (2 in.)50 mm (2 in.) to Unlimitedt to 2t
8.7 NDE of Welds & 8.8 Brittle Fracture Inspection
  • 8.7 NDE of Welds: Prior to welding, groove preparations must be examined with MT or PT. Completed full-penetration welds require 100% volumetric examination (RT or UT). Fillet welds examined with MT or PT.
  • 8.8 Brittle Fracture Inspection: Welds on vessels operating near or below MDMT or subject to temper embrittlement must be inspected for surface-breaking and planar cracking prior to pressurization.
8.9 Rerating Requirements & Code Figures
  • Rerating consists of changing design temperature, MDMT, or MAWP. Requires engineer calculations, inspection, and verification of relief valves.
  • Must follow the exact decision tree of Figure 1.
  • Additional nameplate (Figure 2) must be permanently attached adjacent to original nameplate.
Figure 1 — Rerating Vessels Using the Latest Edition or Addendum of the ASME BPVC Allowable Stresses: Official API 510 flowchart detailing the decision logic for design margins, radiography records, MDMT verification, and pressure testing requirements.
Figure 2 — Sample Additional Nameplate: Required nameplate format for rerated vessels displaying Rerated MAWP, coincident design temperature, minimum design metal temperature (MDMT) at pressure, date of rerating, and Authorized Inspection Agency.
SEC 9

Alternative Rules for Exploration and Production (E&P) Pressure Vessels

Upstream Rules
▼
Upstream Risk Differentiation: Tailored inspection and maintenance rules for exploration and production oilfield vessels, wellhead separators, lease tanks, and treaters categorized into consequence classes (Class 1, 2, and 3).
9.1 Scope & 9.2 Inspection Program Categories
  • Class 1 (High Consequence / Offshore / Populated): External visual inspection every 3 years; Internal/on-stream every 5 years or half remaining life.
  • Class 2 (Medium Risk / Rural Onshore Separators): External visual inspection every 5 years; Internal/on-stream every 10 years or half remaining life.
  • Class 3 (Low Risk / Non-Hazardous): External visual inspection every 10 years; Internal/on-stream every 15 years or half remaining life.
9.3 Pressure Tests, 9.4 Relief Devices & 9.5 Records
  • 9.3 Pressure Testing: When pressure testing is conducted on E&P vessels, testing procedures and temperature safety margins shall comply with Clause 5.8.
  • 9.4 Safety Relief Devices: E&P safety relief valves shall be inspected, tested, and serviced in accordance with Clause 6.6 and API RP 576.
  • 9.5 E&P Records Management:
    • The preferred method is maintaining records per individual vessel; however, grouping by vessel class is permitted where operating conditions and metallurgy are identical.
    • When repairs, alterations, or specific inspections occur, individual vessel records are mandatory.
    • Sample documentation templates from Annex C (Inspection Record) and Annex D (Repair/Alteration/Rerating Form) may be utilized.
ANNEX A

Code Exemptions (Normative)

Scope Boundaries
▼
Exempted Vessels: The following classes of vessels are specifically excluded from API 510 (unless included at owner-operator option).
Complete List of Exemptions
  • 1. Mobile Equipment: Pressure vessels on mobile equipment (trucks, railcars, barges) regulated by DOT or Coast Guard.
  • 2. Low Pressure: Operating pressure not exceeding 103 kPa (15 psig) regardless of size.
  • 3. Machinery Containers: Integral parts or casings of pumps, compressors, turbines, engines, hydraulic/pneumatic cylinders.
  • 4. Small Diameter: Inside diameter, width, height, or cross-section diagonal not exceeding 150 mm (6 in.), with no limit on length or pressure.
  • 5. Water Under Pressure: Vessels containing water with air cushion when design pressure ≤ 2068 kPa (300 psig) AND design temp ≤ 99 °C (210 °F).
  • 6. Hot Water Heaters: Indirectly heated hot water storage tanks when heat input ≤ 200,000 Btu/hr (58.6 kW), water temp ≤ 99 °C (210 °F), and volume ≤ 450 L (120 gal).
  • 7. Small Volume / Pressure Envelopes:
    • Volume ≤ 0.14 m³ (5 cu ft) and design pressure ≤ 1724 kPa (250 psig); OR
    • Volume ≤ 0.04 m³ (1.5 cu ft) and design pressure ≤ 4137 kPa (600 psig).
  • 8. Human Occupancy (PVHO): Pressure chambers for human occupancy (ASME PVHO-1).
  • 9. Fired Heaters: Fired process heaters and furnaces (API 530/573).
  • 10. Piping: Process piping systems (API 570).
ANNEX B

Inspector Certification (Normative)

Certification Rules
▼
Certification Standards: Educational, experience, testing, and recertification requirements for API 510 Authorized Pressure Vessel Inspectors.
Table B.1: Minimum Education and Experience Qualifications
Education LevelMinimum Required Experience in Pressure Equipment
Bachelor of Science degree (or higher) in engineering or technology1 year of design, construction, repair, operation, or inspection experience
2-year technical degree or certificate in engineering or physical sciences2 years of design, construction, repair, operation, or inspection experience
High school diploma or equivalent (GED)3 years of design, construction, repair, operation, or inspection experience
Recertification Cycle:
  • Term is valid for 3 years.
  • Inspectors must document at least 20% of their working time actively performing or supervising API 510 inspection activities within the previous 3 years, or re-take the examination.
  • Web-based online quiz covering code addenda required every 6 years.
ANNEX C-E

Sample Forms and Technical Inquiries

Official Documentation
▼
Standard Documentation: Official API 510 templates for inspection records and repair/alteration/rerating certificates.
Annex C (Informative) — Sample Pressure Vessel Inspection Record: Official template for recording equipment identification, component measurements, CML inspection data, corrosion rates, and inspector certification.
Annex D (Informative) — Sample Repair, Alteration, or Rerating of Pressure Vessel Form: Formal certificate recording scope of repair, welding procedure (WPS), NDE conducted, PWHT applied, pressure test parameters, and sign-offs by the Authorized Inspector and Pressure Vessel Engineer.
Annex E (Informative) — Technical Inquiries

Outlines instructions for submitting formal technical inquiries to the API Committee on Refinery Equipment. Inquiries must specify the exact edition and paragraph, pose a clear question, and provide background with a proposed resolution.
